subject: AI & Agents
title: Self-Driving Cars: From DARPA to Waymo
description: One-minute skill: Self-Driving Cars: From DARPA to Waymo.

hook.text: In 2004, no car finished the DARPA Grand Challenge. In 2024, Waymo drives millions of miles with no driver.

buildup.text: The DARPA challenges in 2004 and 2005 kickstarted autonomous vehicle research.

discovery.text: Stanley, from Stanford, won the 2005 race using LIDAR, cameras, and machine learning.

twist.text: Twenty years later, fully autonomous driving is still limited to specific cities and conditions.

climax.text: Waymo and Cruise operate commercial robotaxis, but universal self-driving remains elusive.

punchline.text: We solved driving in Phoenix. The whole world is much harder.

quiz.question: What happened at the first DARPA Grand Challenge in 2004?
options: No autonomous vehicle finished the course

details.summary: Self-driving cars evolved from DARPA desert challenges in 2004 to Waymo's commercial robotaxi service. The journey spans decades of progress in computer vision, sensor fusion, and decision-making AI.
details.whyItMatters: Autonomous vehicles represent one of AI's most ambitious real-world applications. They promise safer roads but have also revealed how hard it is to deploy AI in safety-critical open environments.
takeaways: Self-driving AI evolved from 2004 DARPA challenges to commercial robotaxis
The technology combines vision, lidar, and reinforcement learning
Full autonomy remains elusive despite decades of progress

faq.question: How close are we to fully autonomous self-driving cars?
faq.answer: Waymo operates commercial robotaxis in several US cities. However, fully autonomous driving in all conditions remains unsolved. Edge cases — unusual weather, erratic drivers, construction — still challenge AI systems.

faq.question: Why has self-driving taken so much longer than predicted?
faq.answer: The real world contains infinite edge cases that are hard to anticipate. Safety requirements are extreme — the AI must be far better than human drivers. Regulatory, liability, and public trust challenges add complexity.
